claimed_coverage: Tests that low-precision Decimal128 arithmetic operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, modulo) do not trigger unnecessary promotion to Decimal256 when the precision boundary calculation shows no overflow would occur.
fix_patch_grounding: The fix in planner.rs adds conditional guards to the Decimal256 promotion logic: for Plus/Minus operations, promotion only occurs when max(s1,s2) + max(p1-s1, p2-s2) >= DECIMAL128_MAX_PRECISION; for Multiply, when p1+p2 >= DECIMAL128_MAX_PRECISION; for Modulo, when max(s1,s2) + max(p1-s1, p2-s2) > DECIMAL128_MAX_PRECISION.
issue_context_used: The issue describes an optimization fix to avoid unnecessary Decimal256 promotion for low-precision Decimal128 operations, improving performance by keeping operations in the more efficient Decimal128 representation when precision allows.
notes: Test inspects the physical plan structure to count Cast nodes to Decimal256. Buggy code creates 2 unnecessary casts (for left and right operands) for low-precision operations. Fixed code only creates casts when precision would actually overflow.
